+from typing import Iterator

+def iter_graphemes(text: str) -> Iterator[str]:
+    """Iterate over the graphemes of a string.
+
+    A grapheme is a sequence of one or more Unicode codepoints that should be
+    treated as a single unit.
+    """
+    if not text:
+        return
+    
+    # This is a simplified grapheme cluster boundary implementation.
+    # In a full implementation, we would follow the Unicode Grapheme Cluster Boundary rules.
+    # For the purpose of this fix, we handle common cases like emojis with modifiers.
+    
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(text):
+        char = text[i]
+        # Start a cluster
+        cluster = char
+        i += 1
+        while i < len(text):
+            # Check if next character is a combining mark or modifier
+            # This is a basic heuristic for grapheme clusters.
+            # Unicode categories: Mn (Mark, Nonspacing), Me (Mark, Enclosing), Mc (Mark, Spacing Combining)
+            # Also include Variation Selectors (U+FE00-U+FE0F) and Skin Tone Modifiers (U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF)
+            next_char = text[i]
+            cp = ord(next_char)
+            # Basic combining characters
+            # 0x0300-0x036F: Combining Diacritical Marks
+            # 0x1AB0-0x1AFF: Combining Diacritical Marks Extended
+            # 0x1DC0-0x1DFF: Combining Diacritical Marks for Symbols
+            # 0x20D0-0x20FF: Combining Diacritical Marks for Symbols and Ligatures
+            # 0xFE00-0xFE0F: Variation Selectors
+            # 0x1F3FB-0x1F3FF: Emoji Modifier Fitzpatrick
+            # 0x1F9B0-0x1F9BF: Emoji Style Modifiers
+            if (0x0300 <= cp <= 0x036F or 
+                0x1AB0 <= cp <= 0x1AFF or 
+                0x1DC0 <= cp <= 0x1DFF or 
+                0x20D0 <= cp <= 0x20FF or 
+                0xFE00 <= cp <= 0xFE0F or 
+                0x1F3FB <= cp <= 0x1F3FF or 
+                0x1F9B0 <= cp <= 0x1F9BF):
+                cluster += next_char
+                i += 1
+            else:
+                break
+        yield cluster
